goal: See that rectangles with the same perimeter can have very different areas, and find which shape gives the most area.
brief: A rectangle is drawn on a grid. Two sliders control Length and Width. A fixed perimeter target (say 20 units) is shown, and as you move one slider the other auto-adjusts to keep the perimeter at 20, while the area and the filled unit squares update live.

controls.label: Length
controls.effect: Increases the rectangle's length; width automatically shrinks to keep perimeter fixed at 20, and the area recalculates and redraws the grid squares.

controls.label: Width
controls.effect: Increases the rectangle's width; length automatically shrinks to keep perimeter fixed at 20, and the area recalculates and redraws the grid squares.

try_this: Make a very long, thin rectangle and watch the area shrink.
Try to make Length equal Width - what happens to the area?
Find the Length/Width pair that gives the biggest area possible.
